body: 1.10 is not supported :( I am actually surprised it did not failed earlier
ok.. then what's the latest version that is under support?
(it's a bit complex but supported 1.10 requires some effort and I need to free some time to work on it.

Hey! @damienmg 

Is there any plan for fixing this problem? As my projects are now greatly depending on it...
So please update me if there is any progress, ok?

Thanks!
Unfortunately we have no fix plan. I do hope to do it by the end of the quarter but it requires diving into the new image format they introduced with 1.10
Got it. Seems can only try other methods, thank you any way!

FWIW the CAS document from docker about the new format: https://gist.github.com/aaronlehmann/b42a2eaf633fc949f93b

the corresponding PR was https://github.com/docker/docker/pull/17924

And relevant bugs about load/save:
https://github.com/docker/docker/issues/20380
https://github.com/docker/docker/issues/18723

The Open Container Initiative has begun creating an image specification (https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec) which is starting from the Docker 1.10 format. The new format seems to add more separation between layers and images with the image configuration file able to reference multiple layer tarballs. 

Taking the above into account, when updating to the new format should a new rule called something like container_build() be created instead? Maybe in order to distinguish between layers and images it could be split into container_layer() and container_image()? I've managed to get Bazel to build images in the OCI format, just wondering what the best way to integrate it would be.
I think sticking with docker_build seems reasonable. Maybe we should just introduce a format attribute to it.
Any chance of this making 0.3.0 or will it not go out until 0.3.1?

Probably not going to be in 0.3.0, We have to recut a canary so we can include it in 0.3.0.

I hope that by 0.3.1 docker rules will be out of bazel.

issue.title: Reconcile with rules_docker?
issue.body:
It looks like this is based on a *really* old fork of [rules_docker](https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_docker) (from when it was bundled with Bazel core).  This is missing out on a significant number of additions/improvements including: `docker_push`, `docker_pull`, as well as some significant speed improvements.

Not sure what your original motivations were for forking, but I'd love to have a conversation about joining forces.  Happy to discuss here, or if you want to reach out to my github handle @google.com
